title: Beauvais Cathedral: The Ambition, Collapse, and Legacy of Gothic Engineering
content: The Cathedral of Beauvais remains one of the most enigmatic and ambitious architectural undertakings of the Gothic era. Conceived to surpass all other cathedrals in height and grandeur, it achieved unprecedented verticality but collapsed under the weight of its own aspirations. This article examines Beauvais as a case study in Gothic engineering—its structural daring, its tragic failures, and its enduring legacy as both inspiration and warning. Through a multidisciplinary lens that combines historical, technical, and philosophical perspectives, we explore how Beauvais challenges our understanding of architectural ambition and human limitation.
